slides.title: Polished is not the same as [credible].
slides.lede: Markets reward signals that reduce uncertainty, and punish signals that look polished without carrying evidence.

slides.title: The test is [differential cost], not price
slides.text: Any firm can pay for an expensive identity, so the expense reveals nothing. Precise, defensible analysis is far easier to sustain with genuine expertise.

slides.title: Does your signal [separate] you or pool you?

cards.label: Separating
cards.text: Different firms choose different actions, so buyers can tell them apart.

cards.label: Pooling
cards.text: Every firm sends the same cue, so buyers learn nothing.

slides.title: Six checks before you [invest in a signal]

items.title: Define the hidden quality
items.text: Cross-border tax expertise, not just quality.

items.title: Identify the receiver
items.text: Procurement, managing partners, founders or referrers.

items.title: Name the observable cue
items.text: What the receiver will actually see.

items.title: Explain the mechanism
items.text: Why it indicates quality, not marketing effort.

items.title: Test imitation risk
items.text: Can a weaker rival copy it cheaply?

slides.title: Five ways a signal [stops working]
slides.note: When a badge becomes common, it can stay visible and still **convey little information**.

slides.quote: A signal is not simply a claim.
slides.text: It is an observable action, attribute or message that changes a receiver's belief about an otherwise unobservable quality.
